text.p: Benfica crushed newly-promoted Setubal 5-1 to lead the Portuguese first division championship on goal difference ahead of familiar rivals Porto and Sporting after three games.

Benfica, who overwhelmed Polish side Ruch Chorzow 5-1 in the Cup Winner's Cup on Thursday, opened the scoring with a goal by midfielder Bruno Caires after a pass from captain Joao Pinto in the 28th minute on Sunday.
Pinto scored the second goal in the 39th minute, Moroccan Nader Hassan scored a third three minutes into the second-half and Romanian midfielder Nica Panduru the fourth in the 84th minute.

Setubal managed a consolation goal five minutes from the end with a shot by striker Paulo Ribeiro, but Brazilian substitute Luis Gustavo quickly restored his side's four-goal margin as beleaguered goalkeeper Candido Rego was beaten for the fifth time.
Reigning champions Porto struggled to secure their 2-0 win over northern side Chaves on Sunday after the excitement of their 3-2 triumph over AC Milan in the Champions League on Wednesday.
Porto opened the score in the 25th minute with a shot by Brazilian winger Edmilson Pimenta from a pass by compatriot Mario Jardel.
Jardel, the hero of the clash with Milan in which he scored two goals, missed several opportunities to score against Chaves, including a penalty in the 52nd minute which hit the bar.
Eventually, three minutes from the end, Porto winger Antonio Folha made the game safe, slamming the ball into the net from a cross by midfielder Rui Barros.
Sporting were in action on Saturday, scoring a 4-3 win at Rio Ave, and now also have seven points from three games. Braga can boast a similar record after a 4-1 win over Gil Vicente.
